I5_01.name: The real man controls his anger
I5_01.text: They're not doing anything haram, Rasulullah knows that, but he was worried about something far deeper. So what does he say? He said, the man amongst you is not the one that can physically put down the other. Any meathead can do that. That's not how we determine who the rajul is. The Prophet is telling him, this is not how we determine men. He said ar-rajul amongst you. The man amongst you. Please, my young brothers, please, don't fall for the fitna of the street, man. This deen will make a man out of you. The street will only make a thug out of you. He said ar-rajul amongst you. The man amongst you is the one When a musiba, when a calamity happens He can control his anger and his wrath. He can control it. He's patient. This is the man.

I5_02.name: One sinner stopped the rain
I5_02.text: And imagine the pressure he was under. My people are turning to me, they're waiting for the response. I'm a prophet of Allah, right? I have direct relationship with Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. Ya Allah, I clearly asked you for rain and nothing happens. Talk about heat under the collar. And he says, Ya Allah, what's happening? I asked for rain and no rain. Listen to what Allah says. He says, Ya Musa, from amongst your people there is one sinner. One. Many sinners are in our towns. Many of our Muslims don't pray. How many of our sisters are still unscarved? How many of our elders still cannot read Fatiha properly? Ya Musa, from amongst your people is one sinner, and because of him and him alone, I have deprived the rain from falling. So you can come to me now and talk to me about justice and wisdom and is this fair all night long. Doesn't change the fact that Allah deprived rain upon a prophet, upon people, upon innocent women and children and animals and crops because of the actions of one man. One man!

I5_03.name: Allah did not expose him
I5_03.text: So Musa waits for the man to come forward. No one comes forward. Musa goes back, asks Allah. To his amazement, the rain comes and starts falling there. So yes, of course Musa's happy the rain is there. Yeah, he's baffled. He's in ajab. He says, Ya Allah, please some clarification. I asked for rain to begin with, you said there's a sinner. I asked for the sinner to come forward, no one came forward. I asked for rain the second time and now the rain comes down. What's going on? Listen to what Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala says to you. He says, Ya Musa, I deprived the rain from coming because of him and him alone. that person, he turned back to me and he asked for my forgiveness. I accepted his tawbah and now because of him and him alone, I've allowed the rain to fall down. So Musa is now interested. He says, oh no. Tell me who this man is. Allah says to Musa, he says, Yeah, Musa, I didn't expose him when he was a sinner. What makes you think I'm gonna expose him now that he's repented and told me?

I5_04.name: Every sin begins with a thought
I5_04.text: He says, every bad habit, every sinful habit begins with a thought. A what? A thought. Whisper comes and goes. If you catch that thought and hold on to it, it turns into an idea. If you hold on to the idea and don't repel it, it turns into A plan. If you hold on to the plan and you don't repel it, it turns into An action. If you repeat the action, the less you feel sensitive towards it and the more normalised it becomes. Then it turns into a habit. And what do habits turn into if you don't deal with them? Addictions. No. The reversal is the same way. Come up with a thought to counter it. Then get an idea, plan it, do an action. Get into the opposite habit again and again and insha'Allah it'll go away.

I5_05.name: You still have hope
I5_05.text: And what happens to you is that you start having a low opinion of yourself. I'm a loser. I'm not worthy. It's true what they say about me. So you start creating these names for yourself and these beliefs. Some people even you start to use religion. to justify their bad thoughts. They say God must hate me. This is a punishment. I make my dua, he doesn't accept it. That means Allah is not pleased with me. Maybe it's because I said this to my mum or my dad. And they start creating so many things which they don't really know about. And sometimes they say, my qadar, the qadar of Allah, is that my life is just bad luck? That's everything's misfortune. That's what Allah has written upon me. No. How do you know Allah has written this upon you? The moment you die, that's it. The moment you're still breathing, it means you have hope. There are doors. Allah doesn't leave you.

I5_06.name: 99% of your fears never happen
I5_06.text: I'm just saying that alhamdulillah, the lesson from that the way to beat your anxiety and depression is to do the opposite. and prove to yourself that you are not what you thought you were. The moment you take those steps other avenues open up. And that is why Rasul said, wala ta'jaz, plan, go ahead, rely on Allah and don't become paralyzed. Keep going. Whatever happens, happens. 99% of our fears never happen. Just think backwards and think how many of your fears actually happened. 99% of them didn't happen. You don't think about them because you forgot about them because nothing happened.

I5_07.name: You are a multi-trillionaire
I5_07.text: One of them, the ungrateful one, he says, I'm poor. I've got nothing to my name. I've been on benefits. I've been on universal credit now for the last five, ten years. I just can't get out of this circle. What do I do? I have nothing. I'm poor. I can't even make ends meet. I can't live like this. But then the happily grateful one says to him, Oh, you're poor, is it? Well give me a price. for your kidneys. How much will you sell them to me for? £10,000, 20,000, what about the price for your liver? How much? £200,000? How much will you sell me your eyesight for? What about your hearing? What about your ability to articulate yourself in a clear and concise way? How much will you sell that for? What about those enzymes that work flawlessly around the clock in your body with no instruction from yourself? How much will you sell them for? What about your epiglottis? That flaps shut that bit of cartilage at the back of your throat when you swallow food or you drink water. If it wasn't for that bit of cartilage, you'd suffocate from any bit of food or water that goes down your windpipe instead of your food pipe. How much will you sell that for? Your ability to go to sleep without injecting yourself or swallowing pills. How much will you sell that for? What about your ability to purify yourself from the bathroom in a dignified and independent way without the help of anybody else? How much will you sell that for? What about the gift of Islam that Allah Almighty has given you free of charge? How the religion is so fair-seeming and beautiful in your eyes, yet your neighbor detests the same religion of yours. How much will you sell that for? So let's put that all together and add it up. Then we see your net worth. You realize you're a multi-trillionaire. But shaitan, he only ever shows us the things that we don't have. And a person like that will stay poor for the rest of his life. Why? Because he's ungrateful. Say, Alhamdulillah. Alhamdulillah.

I5_08.name: Don't wait for the blessing to be taken
I5_08.text: But what I want to say really is, and to leave you with this, don't be that person. Don't be that person who awaits a calamity in his or her life to realize just how indebted you've always been to Allah. Don't wait for a blessing to be withheld from you or even taken away for you then to realize just how blessed you were not too long ago. Don't be that person. Don't be like that person who is trapped into an elevator. He's now breathing damp and hot air. Now he's getting a little bit wheezy and light-headed, and it's getting dangerous. It's critical now, and he's stuck and he's afraid. 30 minutes later, the rescue team comes and the doors open, and he inhales cold, beautiful, pure air and he says, Alhamdulillah, Alhamdulillah, I can breathe again. Alhamdulillah, for the blessing of breathing. Hold on a minute. What are you praising Allah for? What are you thanking Him for? You're thanking him for a blessing that you've had all throughout your life. but it needed to be withheld from you for half an hour.

I5_09.name: No marriage can endure without gratitude
I5_09.text: No marriage can endure and listen to this, my young brothers, my young sisters who are yet to be married and those who are married as well will benefit. No marriage can endure if gratitude is lacking in that relationship. And in my short experience dealing with families who are going through hell from a marital perspective, much of their issues can be traced back to this. There is a lack of gratitude from one or the other or both. And I know you will say that I'm able to give you a long list of negative traits in my wife and my husband. He is this and she is that and he is this and she is that. I know. But then if I was to ask you to enumerate All of the positive traits that you know of your wife or your husband, could you be able to enumerate them? Most of us, if we are honest, will say no. But this is the reality. That you forget that had any other man or woman seen the blessing that you are in with your spouse and whom Allah has placed for you as a wife or a husband, they would fall to their knees behind closed doors, begging Allah Almighty for a fraction of the blessing that you've been blessed with with your wife or husband. But this is the way of shaitan always. With those who are ungrateful, always convincing them that the grass will be somehow greener on the other side. And so eyes wander and gazes are not lowered. And discontentment sets in, and you begin to think, no.

I5_10.name: Allah forgives all sins
I5_10.text: The Shaykh looks at him. He goes, I didn't know what to say to him. I said to him the best verse that I can think of in the Quran. I don't want the guy to hurt himself. There's still hope, insha'Allah. He goes, I just recited, Qul ya ibadiya alladhina asrafu ala anfusihim la taqnatu min rahmatillah. Innallaha yaghfirudh dhunuba jami'a, innahu huwal ghafurur rahim. Say, O Muhammad, to my slaves, who have overburdened themselves with guilt and regret. Do not despair from the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. Allah forgives all sins. He is the most forgiver, the most merciful. The young ahmed looked at the shaykh and he said, Yeah, shaykh. That is true, Allah will forgive everyone but me. I don't deserve to be forgiven. I have shaykhs around me in ulama. I come from a Muslim land of Hajj and Umrah. I'm married, I have children, I have wealth. I know what's halal and haram, and I fell into it. I don't deserve to be forgiven, Ya Shaykh. This is not for me.

I5_11.name: He died in the masjid
I5_11.text: He said, months passed and it was Ramadan. And suddenly, I received a call from his father, the father of Ahmed. He said, Please come quickly. I went to visit him and I knocked on his big door, his palace. And as soon as the father saw me, he burst into tears and began to hug me. I didn't know what was wrong. He said, Your brother, your dear friend Ahmed. He gives you his salaams and he went back to Allah last night. I said to him subhanAllah, I didn't know whether to cry for my friend or for his father. He goes, I went in and it was the Janazah and they had brought the body to the family to farewell the body. He goes, I went inside and the cover sheet was on his face. I took the sheet off Ahmed's face as his dead body lay there and I saw a face. I saw a face that was glittering with shining with light. I saw a face that did not leave this world but had gone to Jannah, insha'Allah. I made dua for him and kissed him on his forehead. His face, and I sat with his father and said, Tell me what happened. He said, He had been going through some sickness which he didn't tell you about. And it was Ramadan. He said, Last night before Maghrib, we were praying together, and I said to him, Son, come and make iftar with us. I said, Dad, I feel like staying at the masjid a little bit longer today. I feel something special. Please leave me for another few minutes. So I left him there. And after iftar, he didn't arrive. So I sent his little brother to go and see him. He was about 10 years old. And the little brother returned back crying, Dad, Dad, Ahmed is not talking. I went to the masjid and I found him reclining on the footsteps of the minbar. As he always does, and he was barely breathing. I rushed to him with the Quran in his hands and I lifted his head onto my shoulders. The father says, I looked and he was trying to say something to me. I came closer and closer because he couldn't make his voice out very well. As he was dying, I knew he was dying. Subhanallah, we called the ambulance. As he was dying, he said, Give my salaams to the shaykh. Give my salaams to the shaykh. And that's why I called you a shaykh to deliver the amanah. He goes, and then suddenly, while he was in my arms,

I5_12.name: Iman is a muscle
I5_12.text: Let me explain to you what the Imam al Bukhari said and let me give it to you in plain English. He said, It is qawlun wa amal. iman is statements and actions. yazidu wa yanqus and it goes up and it goes down. When you say statements and actions. When he says actions, many people think he means iman is a physical action. No. Remember this definition. iman is a muscle. iman is what? A muscle, the gym people are getting very excited. Just relax. iman is a muscle. What does that mean? That means when you work it out, when you exercise it. It increases in strength. And when you don't exercise it. It weakens and it shrinks. The way your bicep size is dependent on your bicep curls, your muscle of iman is dependent on the workout that you do. the actions that you do. What kind of actions are we talking about? Physical actions, like salah, like remembrance of Allah, absolutely. But not just physical actions. iman is dependent on spiritual actions. Spiritual actions. What is a spiritual muscle? Tawakkul, trust in Allah is a muscle. Khawf, fear of Allah is a muscle. The love of Allah is a muscle. These are muscles. If you activate them, if you work on them, you will find that your iman increases. There are spiritual actions and there are physical actions and this is the main thing iman depends on.

I5_13.name: Iman changes how you see the world
I5_13.text: The second way I'll define iman. iman is a world view. Worldview. Worldview means it's how you see the world. For example. Somebody comes, hits your car. Somebody without iman is saying, Oh my gosh, my life is finished. Somebody with iman is saying, Alhamdulillah, Allah sent me someone to test me. This is going to improve my closeness to Him. Day and night difference. Why? It's just the glasses they wear. The iman glasses make you see everything differently. Somebody without iman, they have a child. Where do they head to? Abortion clinic. Why? Let me get rid of this burden. Okay, somebody who has iman gets finds out their wife is expecting. They weren't planning to. They said, Alhamdulillah, blessing from Allah. Why? Of iman, they see the world differently. Somebody without iman, their parents get old, they move far away, their parents say, It would be nice if you came home in some time other than Christmas. They say, Oh my gosh, these parents, what a burden, what an annoyance, what a nuisance. Somebody with iman, their parents call them. They say, Where are you? Before they finish the call, they're outside the door. Why? They see everything differently.

I5_14.name: The forgotten sunnah of solitude
I5_14.text: The Prophet used to love being on his own in order to reflect and think about the creation of Allah. And to just think with clarity. But sometimes you have to escape. You have to book a weekend away in the middle of Wales, in the middle of Yorkshire, in the Peak District, you have to take your family away for two days, for three days. And if you don't do that, a regular practice of that. That was the sunnah of the Messenger. A sunnah that we don't follow anymore. It's the sunnah of escaping from the concrete jungle. Escaping from the markets, escaping from the nine to five. And find a day, find two days, find three days where you are alone in nature with the creation of Allah. and your phone is on airplane mode. That is the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah. What is solitude? Solitude is the ability to be alone. with your own thoughts. Ability to be on your own. in the remembrance of Allah. The ability to not need stimulation, notifications, content, a constant stream of things to keep you distracted.

I5_15.name: We stopped wondering
I5_15.text: They look at nature, they ask questions. Why is a squirrel like that? Why does a camel have a hump? Why is the sky this way? Why are the stars white? Children ask why, why, why? But as you grow up, it gets programmed out of you. You stop wondering. That childish wonder is one of the sunnahs of the Messenger and one of the greatest elements of the fitrah. The instinct the human nature Allah gave us. That wonder must remain with us as we grow older, as we have grey hair, as we have children. Allah wants us to look at His creation and wonder. How did Allah create something so beautiful? And if we have lost this ability to wonder we have lost a core piece of what it means to be a human being. We've lost it. This is the crisis that we have in the world. And if you don't escape the concrete jungle and deliberately spend time in the creation of Allah, you will never regain this part of your heart that has been stolen by the world that we live in. The world of screens, the world of dreams, the world of nine-to-fives, the world of the industrial revolution, the world of concrete. It has extracted from you the part of your fitrah, the part of your heart. That looks at a snowflake and thinks, Subhana Rabbiyal A'la, how amazing is Allah, the one who created.

I5_16.name: When you are stressed, run to the prayer
I5_16.text: When you are in a state of stress, you lost your job, you're stressed, you have family problems, you lost a loved one, your health is deteriorating, what do you do? Fafzaʿu ilas-salah, run to the prayer. That's what you do. Allah told us in the Qur'an. Look for patience. In patience and in prayer, look for aid and support. The Prophet took that verse on. If the Prophet became sad or dumb, Meaning he is distressed. What would he do? He says he would run to the prayer. And he would say the following statement. He will say Arihna biha ya Bilal. Do the adan for us so we can find tranquility through the prayer. Arihna, meaning tuma'nina, tranquility. He would run to the prayer. He would hasten to do sujood and ruku for Allah. The Messenger told us: when you're in sujood, strive.

I5_17.name: If you have these 3 things, you have the world
I5_17.text: The Prophet said, Three things if you have. What are you looking for? Number one. You woke up this morning and you are scared. There's nothing to be scared of. No one's stealing you. No one's robbing you. You're in a safe land. A blessing. And may Allah increase safety for the land of the Muslims. May Allah protect. The lands of the Muslims. Number two. Number two, he is healthy. You're healthy, you have no illness. Number three, you have the food for that day, which is three. That day, not weeks, not months. That day you have the food to eat. Guess what? It's like the whole world has been placed under your feet. What are you looking for? Have those three, it's like the world has been given to your rich man.. Safety. How many people in the world can you see that don't have safety? Any minute they can be bombed and killed. Second is what? You're healthy. Some people are living on what? Medical and tubes in their mouth and etc. Third one is food, rizq something to eat for that day. There are people who don't know what to eat after this meal that they've had, and they haven't had meals for days and months, and they don't know where it's gonna come from. Allah has given you that. You have savings, maybe, and then you said, I lost a job and you're depressed.

I5_18.name: Keep a secret good deed
I5_18.text: So let's say Allah opened up for you. Opportunity to go do some form of charity or to pray qiyam ul-layl or to do this, and then you go and you ruin it. by sharing it and by hoping that people hear about it. Uh yura'i is in the moment, to be seen in the moment. So while you're you're taking into consideration while you're doing something, who's watching and that's going to determine How much you exert yourself. So, if people are watching, I'm gonna stay longer in the sujood, I'm going to add a little bit of. extra spice to this, right? So that people can attribute. a greater level of piety to me than that's actually present inside of me. So The point is is that If Allah opened up for you the opportunity to do something good. And then that good is only known by him. You actually take that as an intimate moment. between you and him an intimate deed. a secret that you hope will come out on the Day of Judgment when other people And and of course all of us have secrets and sins that We hope that Allah will not shame us for on the day of judgment, right? But a secret good deed that you store. Just like with anyone that you love.ve, you do something good and. You know, you want to have some moments that are between you and the person that you love that no one else knows about. It's between you and them. And of course, with the lies, the love is greater. And the one who is sought is greater Subhanahu wa Ta'ala.

I5_19.name: The two hungry wolves
I5_19.text: So let's start with the first one. You know, that hadith about two hungry wolves amongst sheep. So what's the solution? If you have hungry wolves and you have a bunch of sheep, what's the solution? I mean, the solution, if you have hungry wolves and you have sheep. I mean, you protect the sheep. So You can protect the sheep. kill the wolves. You do a little bit of both. Sure. But you need shepherds. So Think of your personality. your makeup as being different sheep. There's a portion of me. So how do I protect this part of me from that wolf? How do I protect this part of me from that wolf? How do I protect this part of me from that wolf? And no one's going to Come and shepherd except for you. You have to be the shepherd of yourself in this regard, right? You have to protect yourself. When the Prophet mentions that, one of the benefits of that hadith Is that the wolves will not stop attacking because the wolves here are. a manifestation of Shaitan. Shaitan is the one that's driving the wolves. The wolves are just manifesting against Shaitan's temptations. Shaitan's not going anywhere. Shaitan will be at you. until the time of your death. And so you can never really kill the wolves. Which means you can never really kill fully the desires themselves.

I5_20.name: Stop caring what people say
I5_20.text: What's the worst that can happen to me? All right, the flip side of that is. What if everybody praises me? What if everybody thinks I'm an amazing person? What if everybody tells me you're the best? What if everybody celebrates me? What really changed about the quality of my life? Did that make me happy? Did that really fulfill me? And then you start realizing like People's perception of you really does not matter that much. And it's a liberating experience when you stop caring about what people say about you. It is so liberating.

I5_21.name: Should I not be a thankful servant?
I5_21.text: And he had many adhkar that he would make in the ruku and the dua and sujood. Making his sujood so long he would stand in the nights till his feet would crack and swell and bleed. And this is the best of mankind. There is not a sin that he's worried about. There is not a, you know, but he loved Allah. Aisha RA told the Prophet, O Messenger of Allah. You don't have any sins on you, and if you did in the past or the future, it would be forgiven. So why? He said, Shouldn't I be abdan shakura?

I5_22.name: Abu Bakr did all this before Fajr
I5_22.text: One day the Prophet finished Fajr Salah. So it's Fajr. And he turned round. And he said, Which one of you? to the Sahaba, give Sadaqah today. Today meaning From the adhan of Fajr. Until the start. They just started, right? From the Adhan? To the iqama of Fajr who gave Sadaqah? Abu Bakr RA said, me, O Messenger of Allah. He said, who visited us sick today? Abu Bakr RA said, me, O Messenger of Allah. Imagine. Yeah, that's like four or five AM. Abu Bakr RA, on his way to the masjid Heard about a sahabi that was ill. Visit them to remind them to come to the masjid or ask about them on the way. On the way, they said, who gave sadaqa today? He said, me. On the way to the masjid, he gave sadaqah. He said, who began this day fasting? Abu Bakr RA said, I did. He said, Who prayed at Janaza today? He said, I did, O Messenger of Allah. Subhanallah, the sahaba radiallahu wanhum. They didn't delay the Janazah. You know, today we somebody dies, no, no, no, no, his grandfather's not here and his uncle's not here, we're gonna wait two weeks, we're gonna k put him in a freezer because his aunt wants to see his body and she's flying in from this country and we're gonna do a open casket and people are gonna come and do all this bidan and give speeches and things. No. So on the way, in early morning, somebody died in the night. When they woke up, they saw that he was dead, they washed his body, they put the thing and they buried him and did the Janazah. Before Fajr Salah and So Abu Bakr RA. Prayed Janazah, woke up fasting, gave sadaqah, visited the sick. Before Fajr. And the Prophet said, Whoever combines these in one day, it's going to be from the people of Jannah.

I5_23.name: Doom scrolling has ruined our generation
I5_23.text: People say I don't have time. They lie. They don't use their time correctly. How can they use the time correctly? Look First thing, what not to do. Doom scrolling has ruined our generations. Just swipe, swipe. People can't even wait for a 30-second video to be over. They're already bored. How will you learn knowledge? How will you learn Quran if you don't have the attention? Don't doom scroll. Second. Don't waste time. with even mubah things. What does that mean? Mubah means maybe they're not haram. Like obviously music and looking at women indecently dressed or women looking at men indecently dressed, that's haram. Yeah. Right? Even things like Even if the aura is covered in things, what benefit? People sit and watch a three hour sports match. And They say they don't have time for Quran. They don't have time for da'wah. People watch Netflix. series for 30 hours that week. Binge watch it, binging it, right? And then they don't have time for Qur'an. People sit and watch. And all these, and make the excuse as if they're doing this for the deen. Instead of watching Ertugrul, why couldn't you read the Quran?

I5_24.name: His legs are heavier than Mount Uhud
I5_24.text: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, the same man who stood and recited Surah Al-Rahman, everybody's attacking him. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud had the thinnest legs in Medina. One day he climbs a tree. and the Sahaba start to make fun of him. They start to laugh at him. Because of the thinness of his calves. It's like a stick. See, what is this? Look at this man. Is this a man or a stick? And they start to laugh at him. And the Prophet tells these men, Half of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. is more heavier in the sight of Allah than the mountain of Uhud. What happened? He didn't do leg day. Huh? He wasn't exercising enough. Yes, he didn't show off his muscles. But there was a muscle that the Prophet appreciated and Allah appreciated more than this. The bravery to stand up for the haqq, for the truth, and not to back down and not to cower away and not to lie and twist and say, No, not really, maybe, but to say the truth as it is.

I5_25.name: Have confidence in Allah first
I5_25.text: Where is his strength coming from? His bravery coming from? It's coming from whom? It's coming from Allah. This is very important. Before you buy all of that nonsense about self-confidence. You need to have confidence in Allah first. That otherwise no speech can help you be self-confident. You imagine somebody standing, climbs up a ladder and they go and they stand on the edge to jump into the swimming pool. They're jumping, jumping, jumping and they turn around. That fear, the mind games at play. The consequences that might have, you don't want to take the plunge because you're scared what's going to happen. And you think that somebody downstairs telling you jump, jump is going to help you? Nobody can give you self-confidence. The first we have to have confidence in Allah. This is the first practical step to have the bravery of the Prophet. We have to have confidence in Allah. When the Prophet is in Hunayn, And all of a sudden thousands of men turn and a sea of arrows is in the air. And all of his companions have turned and run. What's the first thing he says? Allahumma anzil nasrak. Oh Allah, you send me victory and support. My support is gone. First line of defense gone. Second line of defense gone. Midfielders nowhere to be seen. Strikers hiding in the bushes. Oh Allah, I only have you. Send me your help. His confidence is not in himself. He alone is incapable.

I5_26.name: It takes courage to be yourself
I5_26.text: Another great example of the courage of the Prophet is his bravery to be himself. Often, a lot of us we have split personalities. We are somebody else at home. Somebody else at work? Somebody else in the masjid. If you ask someone from work and at home, do you know this guy? They'll say it's two different people. We don't know who this person is. It's very difficult. You need a lot of courage to just be who you are. I used to have a colleague at work. Every day at 12:30, he would tell the colleagues, I'm going for a walk. They think it's strange. Every time we go to eat food, this guy goes for a walk. Every day he goes for a walk. He comes back 25 minutes later: rain, sun, snow. I knew obviously he's going to pray salah. So I asked him one day, listen, Habibi, why don't you just tell them? I'm going to pray. Maybe one of them will start asking you questions about Islam. Why don't you just be yourself? You know what he said? He said, I'm scared, what will they think of me? To be yourself takes courage. I remember the first time. First time I came to the UK, I came I went to university in Nottingham and A Muslim person came and introduced himself to me. He goes, Hey, my name's Mo. My first time in the UK, I'm thinking, what is wrong with this guy? He can see me. You know, I just prayed salah. I came, we saw each other in the prayer room, we saw each other in the muslim. He knows I'm a Muslim. Hey, my name is Mo. What's going on? I observed this man over time. I even remember in Ramadan he would say, I'm not feeling hungry. Allah, poor guy. What a great diet he's on. And he would never reveal himself to those around him. Why? Why? Why? I'm scared. I am fearful what will happen if they know who I am. What's the consequence? Will they exclude me? Will they treat me differently? Will they look at me differently? Will I not get the same privileges I used to get? There is this fear, there is this uncertainty. It requires bravery and courage to stand up and say this is who I am.

I5_27.name: Put Allah first and He will move mountains
I5_27.text: You see what happens when you put Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala first? Allah will move mountains for you. The same Allah that split the moon for who? The Prophet Muhammad. The same Allah that split the ocean for Musa. And these were prophets and they are up here. And don't get me wrong. Their status and their honour is more than us. But  They were still human. They were human like us. So the same Allah that establishes these miracles for them is the same Allah that establishes these miracles for me. How did He do that miracle for me? I'll tell you how. I was once upon a time thinking that I could go out of my way to displease Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, to displease my parents, harming other people. It got me nowhere. Making money, the money that I was making, the money the man them around me were making, Akhi was getting us somewhere. The fame that came with it. The girls that came with it. The cars that came with it. Akhi, you name it. It was happening. But we was always miserable. The reason why we was miserable because we was neglecting and delaying Salah.

I5_28.name: You could be the next Salahuddin
I5_28.text: Look at what happened to Salahuddin Ayyubi. He was a man that conquered Jerusalem. He's a man that opened the doors of Jerusalem. Achi, in his teenage years, he wasn't even practicing. He wasn't the best of Muslims, bro. He probably forgot about Salah, neglected Salah, delayed Salah. And whatever he was getting up to, he was getting up to, bro. But the reality is, when he changed, when he became obedient to Allah, when he became under the people of knowledge and established the basics of Islam in his life. Allah used him as a tool. And what was that bro? He opened the doors of Jerusalem. You are that person. And I'm not saying we're in the situation we're in today. But you could be the one to be the future leader, Akhi. If it's not in our communities, Akhi, then the leaders of the world. Wallahi do not belittle the reward that Allah will send your way. When you give up something for the sake of Allah, if it's a haram relationship, if it's weed, If it's making haram money, my brother, if you give it up for the sake of Allah, Allah will bring the world at its knees to you, for you. Wallahi, I've been, I've been, I've experienced this. When I've given up certain things for the sake of Allah Akhi. Wa Allahi Allah sends me so much opportunity, so much doors that are opening up for me, Akhi I'm like, I don't know which door to take, Ya Allah. I don't know. You pray istikhara and you think to yourself, Alhamdulillah, this is the best option for me. But Allah will do that for you.

I5_29.name: Tahajjud is my weapon
I5_29.text: I'll say to him, Achi, what's your how is it that you've been stabbed over a hundred times, and you're still alive? How, bro? Like you've got scars everywhere. He says to me, I never, ever, ever leave Tahajjud. He never ever misses Tahajjud. He said, Tahajjud is my weapon. Other than my five daily prayers, Tahajjud is my weapon. Tahajjud is my protection. Tahajjud is what gets me through the day. Salatul Tahajjud is what makes me feel alive, Ahi. Why? 'Cause Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala comes to the lowest level of heaven. And he asks you Where are my servants that are the ones that are asking? for me. Where are those that are gonna be raising their hands? And making dua in order for me to give them, in order for me to make their hands return back to them, and me giving them what they ask for. Where are my servants, bro? Imagine that. Allah speaking to you. And when Allah is speaking to you, He says, Ya ibadi. He doesn't say to you, Oh servants, He goes, Ya ibadi, O my servants.
